answer: Let a key's weight be the square of the copper it holds; each operator runs one cedar that every epoch burns one sable into one copper credited to a single chosen key, never per key. A lone honest key reaches weight r² after r cedar epochs and r sable. The kth clone of that operator must add r further epochs and r further sable on that same cedar, so n clones cost n·r sequential epochs and n·r sable: minting cannot be parallelised, splitting copper across keys only lowers the squared weight, and extra cedars simply begin again as unknown newcomers.
